project.title: Launch of a Nutritious Home-Delivered Meal Service for Seniors
project.objective: Design and pilot a weekly home-delivered meal and basic care support service for older adults living at home, focused on nutrition, safety, and independence.
deliverables: Weekly rotating menu tailored to older adults' dietary needs
Standard operating procedures for meal prep, packing, and delivery
Home visit checklist covering nutrition, hygiene, and safety checks
Pilot schedule and route plan for 20 initial clients
Incident and escalation protocol for health or safety concerns
Training brief for cooks and home care aides on the new service
constraints: All meals must comply with food safety and hygiene regulations
Menu must support common dietary restrictions (low salt, diabetes-friendly)
Home visits limited to 30 minutes per client per day
Service must operate within existing kitchen equipment and staffing
Pilot must be ready to start within 21 days
Documentation must be simple enough for quick use during visits

risks.risk: Meals do not meet specific dietary needs of some older adults.
risks.mitigation: Have dietitian review menu and add clear labels and simple substitution options.

risks.risk: Home care aides run out of time during visits and skip key checks.
risks.mitigation: Create a short prioritized checklist and timebox each step; test in a dry run.

risks.risk: Food safety issues during transport to clients' homes.
risks.mitigation: Define packing and temperature control steps and add a quick transport checklist.

risks.risk: Cooks and home care aides misunderstand new procedures.
risks.mitigation: Run a short joint training session and keep procedures in a one-page guideline.

risks.risk: Clients resist changes to their usual meals or routines.
risks.mitigation: Include a feedback step in first week visits and allow small menu adjustments.

themes.why_relevant: Menus and visit routines must support health conditions like diabetes and hypertension.

themes.theme: Food safety and hygiene in home delivery
themes.why_relevant: Safe preparation, packing, and transport are critical to protect vulnerable clients.
Home care aides must balance meal delivery, checks, and support within short visits.
Clients need clear explanations and choice about meals and home support tasks.
Staff must know how to react if they see health, safety, or nutrition issues at home.

backlog.task: Draft a 2-week rotating menu suitable for older adults with common dietary needs
definition_of_done: Menu includes breakfast, lunch, and dinner options for 14 days
Each meal has a brief note on dietary suitability (e.g. low salt, soft food)
Menu reviewed and adjusted based on dietitian feedback
Menu stored in shared folder and referenced in service documents

backlog.task: Define standard recipes and portion sizes for all menu items
definition_of_done: Each menu item has a simple recipe with ingredients and steps
Portion sizes are defined and tested for older adults
Food safety steps are clearly marked in each recipe
Recipes compiled into a single document for kitchen use

backlog.task: Create a home visit checklist for meal delivery and basic care checks
definition_of_done: Checklist covers meal delivery, eating ability, hydration, and mood
Includes quick home safety and hygiene observations
Fits on one page and can be completed in under 5 minutes
Reviewed and approved by operations manager or equivalent

backlog.task: Design a simple incident and escalation flow for issues found at home
definition_of_done: Common incident types are listed (health, safety, nutrition, hygiene)
Clear steps defined for who to inform and how fast
Template for incident notes is created
Flow shared with cooks and home care aides in training

backlog.task: Define packing and transport procedure to keep meals at safe temperature
definition_of_done: Packing steps documented from kitchen to delivery departure
Temperature control method defined and feasible with current equipment
Quick pre-departure checklist created for drivers or aides
Procedure tested once with sample meals

backlog.task: Draft a short script to explain the new service to clients during first visit
definition_of_done: Script explains purpose, what clients can expect, and how to give feedback
Language is simple and respectful, with space for questions
Includes how to handle refusal or concerns
Script reviewed by operations manager or equivalent

backlog.task: Plan the pilot schedule and daily route for 20 initial clients
definition_of_done: List of 20 pilot clients with preferred delivery windows
Daily route order drafted to fit within working hours
Buffer time included for delays and incidents
Schedule shared with kitchen so prep times align

backlog.task: Prepare a joint training brief for cooks and home care aides
definition_of_done: Key changes in kitchen and visit routines summarized on 1-2 pages
Includes menu overview, safety points, and incident flow
Training agenda with timing drafted
Brief shared in channel before training session

backlog.task: Run a dry run of one full delivery route with test meals
definition_of_done: At least 5 stops simulated with timing recorded
Packing, transport, and visit checklist used end-to-end
Issues and delays documented
Adjustments proposed for schedule or procedures

backlog.task: Define cleaning and equipment temperature check routine for kitchen
definition_of_done: List of daily and weekly cleaning tasks created
Temperature check steps and frequency defined
Simple log template prepared for recording checks
Routine validated against food safety requirements

backlog.task: Set up a simple client feedback log for first month of the pilot
definition_of_done: Log format created to capture meal satisfaction and issues
Home care aides know when and how to ask for feedback
Plan defined to review feedback weekly
Log accessible to both cooks and aides

backlog.task: Summarize pilot readiness status and open issues before launch
definition_of_done: Checklist of all key tasks reviewed against completion
Open issues and risks listed with owners
Go/no-go recommendation drafted
Summary shared in channel two days before launch

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on menu, recipes, and food safety steps for the pilot.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message announcing the new home-delivered meal service project.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the initial 2-week menu and recipe set for the pilot.
Agree on final food safety and packing procedure before testing.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define visit workflow, checklist, and incident handling.
threads_plan.trigger: Home care aide shares first draft of the home visit checklist.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Lock the final version of the home visit checklist for the pilot.
Confirm the incident reporting and escalation flow to use during visits.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Plan routes, schedule, and dry run for the pilot deliveries.
threads_plan.trigger: First draft of the pilot client list and route plan is posted.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the daily route and schedule for the 20 pilot clients.
Decide on any adjustments after the dry run before launch.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on training content and readiness before launch.
threads_plan.trigger: Cook posts the draft training brief and asks for final comments.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm the joint training agenda and materials for cooks and aides.
Make a final go/no-go decision for starting the pilot on the planned date.

channel_rituals: Daily async check-in each morning with planned visits, kitchen prep focus, and risks.
End-of-day summary noting incidents, client feedback, and any menu or route issues.
Weekly pilot review message to discuss feedback log and propose adjustments.
Pre-launch and mid-pilot mini-retrospective to capture what to change quickly.
